segmentation.text: It is unlawful for any person to drive or operate
a vehicle of any kind or character
in a careless or imprudent manner
on any highway
in the City

elements.justification: 'drive or operate' names who controls the vehicle, which no atom observes; per the ontology's section on what is not an atom it is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, 'a vehicle moving on the road is taken to be driven'. kin.speed, 'magnitude of velocity', tells the moving vehicle (speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) from one at rest; it is used for motion, not as a stand-in for acceleration or a manoeuvre. 'any person' is the one who drives: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever controls it.

'vehicle' is a defined term of this law with the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle: '“Vehicle” means every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway', with its exceptions (human-powered devices, electric bicycles, EPAMDs, electric scooters) made by the reading's classification. 'of any kind or character' adds no restriction and removes none beyond the definition; the aggregate is one atom and is not expanded.

Same words and meaning as the index's 'on a highway' -> rel.occupies, st.highway. st.highway: 'the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders', which is the defined 'entire width between the boundary lines of every way dedicated to a public authority'; it is not the roadway, and the words do not narrow to the roadway. rel.occupies: 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region' anchors the subject on that highway.

operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: driving is read as careless or imprudent where, while the subject moves, it collides with another road user (rel.contact) or another road user's centre and the subject's, under constant velocities, approach within p.conflict_horizon to a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (a critical conflict). Care is a state of mind and the whole duty is this standard, so the rule is a surrogate.

assumptions.meaning: the place of the road user at the observation lies within the territorial limits of the incorporated city whose ordinances the reading applies, as the map's reading classifies the area

applicability: The subject is a member of the vehicle aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, its footprint occupies a highway region (st.highway), asm.within_city_limits holds at the observation, and the subject is moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance).
obligation: No other road user u of the scene (any class) is in contact with the subject (rel.contact), and no other road user u is such that, under constant velocities, the subject's and u's centres approach within p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) to a closest-approach centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance). Surrogate: the verdict is evidence of carelessness, not a legal conclusion.

narrowings.why: 'drive or operate' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: a moving vehicle is taken to be driven, whoever or whatever controls it.

'careless or imprudent' is read only through a collision or a critical conflict with another road user; careless conduct that produces neither (inattention, erratic lane keeping with no one near, harsh braking) is not read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject car moves at 15 m/s on a highway inside the city (asm.within_city_limits declared true) toward a car halted ahead in its lane; at 2 s from the closest approach the projected centre distance is 1 m, and it does not brake.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The subject car moves at 12 m/s alone on a city highway; no other road user is in the scene, so no contact and no conflict exist.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject car moves in a private parking lot that is no highway region; it occupies no st.highway.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The subject car moves on a city street close behind a slower car with a projected conflict, but the source does not observe region occupancy, so whether it is on a highway is unknown.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of road-user tracking in recorded and simulated traces

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
param_proposals.source: traffic-conflict technique (Swedish TCT, Hydén 1987): time-to-collision thresholds of 1.5 to 3 s

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
param_proposals.source: AASHTO passenger-car design vehicle dimensions (about 5.8 m by 2.1 m)

segmentation.text: No person shall ride or drive
any vehicle
over or across any pavement newly laid or repaired
across or around which there has been placed a barrier
or at or near which there is a person or a sign warning persons against riding or driving over such pavement
or a sign stating that the highway is closed
The provisions of this Section shall not apply to the employees actually engaged in the paving or repair of such pavement

elements.justification: 'ride or drive' names who controls the vehicle and is read through its controlled motion ('a vehicle moving on the road is taken to be driven'): kin.speed, 'magnitude of velocity', above p.halt_speed_tolerance; rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region', carries 'over or across' the pavement region bound in a3.

'vehicle' is a defined term of this law with the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'); claimed as one atom, never expanded.

Nearest atoms only (the span carries a gap): st.roadway, 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic', is where pavement lies but carries no attribute of its surface being newly laid or repaired; dev.temporary_traffic_control, 'cones, barricades, temporary signs and flashers marking works, a closure or an obstruction', marks works but not that the surface it marks is fresh pavement. Neither denotes 'pavement newly laid or repaired'.

A barrier placed across or around the pavement is a barricade: dev.temporary_traffic_control, 'cones, barricades, temporary signs and flashers marking works, a closure', tied to the pavement's travel region by dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls'; governance, not distance, ties the barrier to the stretch it closes. Not a stand-in for a position: the rule does not read where a halt is required from it.

A person warning persons against driving over the pavement is dev.human_direction, 'a person directing traffic and the direction given', role flagger, indication stop; a warning sign is a temporary sign of dev.temporary_traffic_control or a dev.regulatory_sign of code closed_to_traffic. 'at or near which' ties the device to the pavement through dev.governs (the device controls the pavement's travel region), not through a distance.

dev.regulatory_sign, 'a point regulation by catalogue code', code closed_to_traffic, is a sign stating that the highway is closed; dev.governs ties it to the travel region it closes. A prohibition sign is a condition, not a manoeuvre, as its contract says.

Nearest atom only (the span carries a gap): ru.official_vehicle, 'a vehicle in official or contracted road service, identifiable by livery or equipment', kind highway_maintenance, states what a road user is, not that it is 'actually engaged in the paving or repair of such pavement': a maintenance vehicle passing through is not engaged, and a contractor's unmarked vehicle may be. No atom records the work a road user is doing at a place.

applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, is not engaged in the paving or repair of that pavement (the gap ru.road_work_activity), and a stretch of newly laid or repaired pavement p (the gap's region) is in the scene that a barricade (dev.temporary_traffic_control), a flagger signalling stop (dev.human_direction), a warning sign or a closed_to_traffic regulatory sign governs (dev.governs).
obligation: The subject does not occupy (rel.occupies) the pavement p while moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance).

narrowings.why: 'ride or drive' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion over the pavement.

'at or near which there is a person or a sign warning' is read as a flagger or a sign governing the pavement's travel region; a warning sign that the source records as governing no region does not trigger the duty.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car drives at 8 m/s over a lane of fresh asphalt that a row of barricades governs.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A car drives in the open adjacent lane while barricades govern the lane of fresh asphalt; its footprint never overlaps the fresh pavement.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car drives on an ordinary street with no barricade, flagger or closure sign and no fresh pavement in the scene.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A car drives over a lane of fresh asphalt beside barricades, but the source does not observe which region the barricades govern.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A paving crew's roller, recorded as engaged in paving that stretch, drives over the barricaded fresh asphalt.

gaps.proposal: `st.fresh_pavement` | a stretch of pavement newly laid or repaired and not yet open to travel (uncured asphalt or concrete, fresh surfacing), carried as a region with a reference point and a boundary; it decides where a vehicle may not travel **Not a stand-in for:** a work zone or the devices marking it (`dev.temporary_traffic_control`), or an object on the road (`st.obstruction`) — a closure marks a place, not the state of its surface | general
gaps.nearest: st.roadway ('the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic': no attribute of the surface's age); dev.temporary_traffic_control ('cones, barricades, temporary signs and flashers marking works, a closure or an obstruction': marks works, not that the surface is newly laid); st.obstruction (kinds debris, excavation, barrier: an object, not the surface)

gaps.proposal: `ru.road_work_activity` | the road user is engaged, at the observation, in work on the way at its place: paving, surfacing, repair or maintenance of the roadway or of the right-of-way, as the source records the activity; it decides which road users a closure of works does not bind **Not a stand-in for:** the class of a works or maintenance vehicle (`ru.official_vehicle`) — a maintenance vehicle passing through is not engaged in the work, and a contractor's unmarked vehicle may be | general
gaps.nearest: ru.official_vehicle ('a vehicle in official or contracted road service, identifiable by livery or equipment', kind highway_maintenance): a class, which states what the vehicle is, not the work it is doing at the place

segmentation.text: The City Traffic Engineer is authorized to determine and designate those heavily traveled streets
upon which shall be prohibited the use of the roadway
by motor-driven cycles, bicycles, horse-drawn vehicles or other nonmotorized traffic
and shall erect appropriate signs giving notice thereof
When signs are erected giving notice thereof
no person shall disobey the restriction stated on such signs

elements.justification: The designation of a street is a legal status no scene shows; the ontology reads the legal status of a feature through the feature's presence: the regulatory sign (dev.regulatory_sign, 'a point regulation by catalogue code') governing the street's roadway (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls'; st.roadway, 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic'). 'heavily traveled' is the engineer's criterion for designating, which the posted sign presumes.

'the use of the roadway' is presence on it: rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region', on st.roadway, 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder', which is the defined 'portion of a highway which is improved and ordinarily used for vehicular traffic, exclusive of the shoulder'. Not the sidewalk or shoulder.

Nearest atoms (the span carries gaps): 'bicycles' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle ('a device propelled by human power upon which a person may ride'); 'motor-driven cycles' (no definition applies) are ru.moped / ru.motorcycle; 'other nonmotorized traffic' is the traffic aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances') read with the qualifier nonmotorized. The sign's restriction is dev.regulatory_sign, 'a point regulation by catalogue code', code bicycles_prohibited or nonmotorized_prohibited (a horse-drawn vehicle being nonmotorized traffic); no class atom denotes a horse-drawn vehicle, so whether a road user is one the nonmotorized prohibition binds cannot be read (the gap). The code catalogue states no prohibition of motor-driven cycles; that is reported to the operator.

'appropriate signs giving notice thereof' are read through their presence (status): a dev.regulatory_sign of a restricting code governing (dev.governs) the designated roadway. The engineer's duty to erect them binds no road user; what it adds for the road user is the sign's presence.

'When signs are erected giving notice thereof': a dev.regulatory_sign whose code states the restriction governs (dev.governs) a roadway (st.roadway); the sign is a condition, not a manoeuvre, per its contract.
Disobeying the restriction is using the roadway the sign governs while being of the class it prohibits: rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region', on that st.roadway.

applicability: A regulatory sign of code bicycles_prohibited, nonmotorized_prohibited, or a motor-driven-cycle or animal-drawn-vehicle prohibition (the gaps) governs a roadway r of the scene, and the subject, a member of DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, is of the class that sign prohibits.
obligation: The subject does not occupy the roadway r the sign governs.

narrowings.why: the designation of the street by the City Traffic Engineer is read through the presence of the posted sign governing its roadway.
'appropriate signs' are read through their presence; their adequacy is presumed.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A cyclist rides on a roadway governed by a bicycles_prohibited regulatory sign.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A cyclist rides on a separate path beside a roadway governed by a bicycles_prohibited sign; its footprint never overlaps that roadway.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A cyclist rides on a roadway that no restricting regulatory sign governs.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A cyclist rides on a roadway beside a bicycles_prohibited sign, but the source does not observe which region the sign governs.

gaps.proposal: `ru.animal_drawn_vehicle` | a vehicle drawn by a horse or another animal (a carriage, cart or wagon), together with the animals drawing it; it decides which road users a restriction of the roadway concerns **Not a stand-in for:** a trailer drawn by a motor vehicle (`ru.trailer_or_combination`) or a ridden animal | general
gaps.nearest: ru.trailer_or_combination ('vehicle drawn by another, or the combination': drawn by a vehicle, not by an animal); ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic (the aggregate's classes include no animal-drawn vehicle to classify)

segmentation.text: Except as otherwise provided in Subsection (B)
it is unlawful to operate
a motorized vehicle
upon or within a right-of-way that:
(1) Has been designated on an official trails plan as an equestrian trail, multi-use trail, or other trail not intended for use by motorized vehicles;
(2) Has been dedicated to the City for use as such a trail;
and (3) Has been posted with appropriate signs to indicate that motorized vehicles are prohibited.
The provisions of Subsection (A) do not apply to: (1) An emergency vehicle;
(2) Any vehicle that is being used in connection with maintenance of the right-of-way;
or (3) Any motorized wheelchair or other device that is designed for and used by a mobility-impaired person.

elements.justification: 'operate' names who controls the vehicle and is read through its controlled motion ('a vehicle moving on the road is taken to be driven'): kin.speed, 'magnitude of velocity', above p.halt_speed_tolerance. Same reading as the index's 'when operating a vehicle' -> kin.speed.

'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'). The law's own word 'motorized' limits which members the duty reads: it leaves out vehicles with no motor (animal-drawn vehicles, trailers by themselves). The motorized classes are ru.motor_vehicle ('a self-propelled vehicle other than a rail vehicle'), the powered two-wheelers it excludes and classes separately (ru.motorcycle 'motor vehicle on two or three wheels', ru.moped 'a low-power two- or three-wheeler with a small engine or motor'), and the classes whose contracts make them motor vehicles or powered passenger and goods vehicles (ru.bus, ru.transit_bus, ru.school_bus, ru.truck, ru.taxicab, ru.tour_bus_or_limousine, ru.commercial_motor_vehicle). The aggregate stays the class; the classes are the qualifier beside it.

'upon or within a right-of-way' places the subject on a strip of way: rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region', on a travel region (st.travel_region, the union of the kinds a device can govern), the region the posted sign of c7 governs. The right-of-way's legal character is carried by c5-c7.

dev.regulatory_sign, 'a point regulation by catalogue code', code motor_vehicles_prohibited, is a sign indicating that motorized vehicles are prohibited; dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls', ties it to the region the subject occupies. 'appropriate' and 'posted' are legal status, read through the sign's presence.

ru.emergency_vehicle, 'vehicle of a class the jurisdiction designates as emergency'. The words name the class alone, not a responding emergency vehicle, so the exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: a responding emergency vehicle' does not apply.

Nearest atom only (the span carries a gap): ru.official_vehicle, 'a vehicle in official or contracted road service, identifiable by livery or equipment', kind highway_maintenance or municipal, states what a vehicle is, not that it 'is being used in connection with maintenance of the right-of-way': a maintenance vehicle using the trail as a shortcut is not, and a contractor's unmarked truck may be. No atom records the work a road user is doing at a place.

assumptions.meaning: the place of the road user at the observation lies within a right-of-way that an official trails plan designates as an equestrian trail, a multi-use trail or another trail not intended for use by motorized vehicles, as the map's reading records
the right-of-way at the place of the road user at the observation has been dedicated to the city for use as a trail, as the map's reading records

residues.why: Subsection (B) is the text's own exception list, carried by c8-c10; the reference adds no restriction of its own, so the duty is the same whether or not its words are read.

A motorized wheelchair or other device designed for and used by a mobility-impaired person carries its user as a pedestrian (the pedestrian definition: 'a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair'); such a device carries none of the motorized vehicle classes the subject must carry (c3), so the duty is the same whether or not the exception is read.

applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle and carries one of the motorized classes (ru.motor_vehicle, ru.motorcycle, ru.moped, ru.bus, ru.transit_bus, ru.school_bus, ru.truck, ru.taxicab, ru.tour_bus_or_limousine, ru.commercial_motor_vehicle); it is not an ru.emergency_vehicle, and it is not being used in maintenance of the right-of-way (the gap ru.road_work_activity); its footprint occupies a travel region r (st.travel_region) that a dev.regulatory_sign of code motor_vehicles_prohibited governs (dev.governs); and asm.designated_trail and asm.trail_dedicated_to_city hold at the observation.
obligation: The subject is not moving: its kin.speed is at or below p.halt_speed_tolerance while it occupies that region r.

narrowings.why: 'operate' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: a motorized vehicle moving on the trail is operated; one at rest there is not.

'posted with appropriate signs' is read through the presence of a motor_vehicles_prohibited regulatory sign governing the region the subject occupies; a trail the source maps as no travel region, or whose sign it records as governing nothing, does not engage the duty.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A motorcycle rides at 6 m/s on a path governed by a motor_vehicles_prohibited sign; the trace declares asm.designated_trail and asm.trail_dedicated_to_city true.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A car stands at rest (speed 0) on the same signed trail path, both assumptions declared true.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car drives on an ordinary street that no motor_vehicles_prohibited sign governs.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A car is on the signed trail path with both assumptions declared true, but its speed is not observed.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: An ambulance (ru.emergency_vehicle) drives at 5 m/s on the signed trail path, both assumptions declared true.

segmentation.text: Whenever any vehicle is stopped at a marked crosswalk or at any unmarked crosswalk at an intersection to permit a pedestrian to cross the roadway
the driver of any other vehicle
approaching from the rear shall not overtake and pass such stopped vehicle

elements.justification: 'any vehicle' is a member b of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, quantified in the rule. 'is stopped' is drv.motion.complete_halt on b ('at rest at the observation', speed at or below p.halt_speed_tolerance). 'at a marked crosswalk or at any unmarked crosswalk at an intersection' is a crosswalk c: st.crosswalk, 'marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection', which is the defined crosswalk in both of its branches; b is at c where its body occupies c (rel.occupies) or lies within p.stop_point_tolerance of it (st.region_geometry, 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it'), and c lies ahead of or under b along the direction of a carrier b occupies (prim.region_offset_along not negative; carrier of kind st.travel_region): a vehicle halted beyond the crossing is not stopped at it. 'to permit a pedestrian to cross the roadway' is a purpose, read through the conduct it explains: a pedestrian (DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian, 'a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair') occupies the crosswalk c (rel.occupies) at the same observation.

'the driver of any other vehicle' names the vehicle whose conduct is judged, a member of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle other than b; same mapping as the index's 'The driver of a vehicle'. 'driver' is a role, read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

'approaching from the rear ... overtake and pass such stopped vehicle' is the manoeuvre of drv.interaction.overtake_pass(subject, b): the subject, travelling in the same direction as b, comes from having b ahead of it (approaching from the rear) to having b behind it. 'such stopped vehicle' is the same b bound by the trigger.

applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, and some other vehicle b of the scene (DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, not the subject) is, at the observation or at some observation of the p.overtake_window behind it, at a complete halt (drv.motion.complete_halt with p.halt_speed_tolerance) at a crosswalk c (its body occupying c or within p.stop_point_tolerance of c, with c not behind it along the direction of a carrier it occupies) while a pedestrian occupies c.
obligation: There is no other vehicle b such that, at the observation, the subject overtakes and passes b (drv.interaction.overtake_pass(subject, b) with window p.overtake_window and same_dir_cos p.overtake_same_direction_cos, at its recognition) and the trigger held for b at some observation of that act: from the last observation of the window behind at which b was ahead of the subject with headings aligned, up to the observation itself, b was at a complete halt at a crosswalk c occupied by a pedestrian, as stated in the applicability.

narrowings.why: 'to permit a pedestrian to cross the roadway' is a purpose, read through the conduct it explains: the vehicle is halted at the crosswalk while a pedestrian occupies that crosswalk; a halt for a pedestrian still waiting on the curb is not read.
'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the overtaking vehicle whoever controls it.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Car b halts 1 m before a marked crosswalk in the right lane while a pedestrian walks on the crosswalk; the subject car, coming up behind b in the same direction, moves to the left lane and passes b within 6 s while b is still halted and the pedestrian still on the crosswalk.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Car b halts before a marked crosswalk with a pedestrian on it; the subject car, behind b in the same direction, halts behind b and does not pass it.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject car drives along a street; no vehicle is halted at any crosswalk, and no other vehicle is in the scene.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Car b stands before a marked crosswalk with a pedestrian on it while the subject passes it, but the speed of b is not observed, so whether b is stopped is unknown.

scenarios.name: occasion_d1
scenarios.narrative: Car b is halted at an unmarked crosswalk at an intersection with a pedestrian on it during the first 3 s of the subject's pass; the pedestrian then reaches the far curb and b remains halted while the subject completes the pass 2 s later.

scenarios.name: occasion_d1_outside
scenarios.narrative: Car b halts at a marked crosswalk with a pedestrian on it while the subject waits behind; the pedestrian clears the crosswalk and b moves off before the subject begins to move out; the subject passes b, which is then moving, 8 s later, with no pedestrian on the crosswalk during the pass.

under_way.justification: An observation inside the pass is one at or after the last observation of the window behind at which b was ahead of the subject with headings aligned (rel.bearing longitudinal component positive, rel.longitudinal_overlap negative, rel.same_direction within p.overtake_same_direction_cos), at which the subject is moving (kin.speed, 'magnitude of velocity', above p.halt_speed_tolerance), and before b is behind the subject: it is read from the subject's motion and the two road users' relative position, not from the region either occupies.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of road-user tracking in recorded and simulated traces

param_proposals.name: p.stop_point_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the body-to-mark gap within which a halt counts as at the mark: a stop line's set-back before a crossing plus a placement margin
param_proposals.source: MUTCD section 3B.16: stop lines placed at least 4 ft in advance of the nearest crosswalk line

param_proposals.name: p.overtake_window
param_proposals.convention: the longest duration of an overtaking manoeuvre on an urban street, from having the overtaken vehicle ahead to having it behind
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book passing-manoeuvre model: passing times of about 4 to 11 s

param_proposals.name: p.overtake_same_direction_cos
param_proposals.convention: cosine of the largest heading difference (about 25 degrees) at which two vehicles count as travelling in the same direction while one moves out to pass the other
param_proposals.source: heading angles of urban lane changes, typically below 20 degrees

segmentation.text: No pedestrian
shall cross a roadway
at any place other than by a route at right angles to the curb or by the shortest route to the opposite curb
except in a crosswalk

elements.justification: 'pedestrian' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'); one atom, never expanded.

Crossing a roadway is being on it and moving across it: rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region', on st.roadway, 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder' (the defined roadway; not the sidewalk or shoulder), and drv.motion.moving_across_carrier(subject, k) with cos_max p.crossing_motion_cos on a carrier k the pedestrian occupies (a lane, st.lane, or the roadway itself), whose designated direction is the direction the curbs run: moving across, not along, the way. Walking along the roadway is not crossing it.

'a route at right angles to the curb' is motion at right angles to the direction the roadway's carriers run, which is the curb's direction: drv.motion.moving_across_carrier(subject, k) with cos_max p.right_angle_crossing_cos, the tolerance of 'at right angles' on sampled headings. 'the shortest route to the opposite curb' between curbs that run parallel is the same perpendicular route.
st.crosswalk, 'marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection', is the defined crosswalk; rel.occupies places the pedestrian in it. Not a sidewalk.

applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian, occupies a roadway (st.roadway), does not occupy a crosswalk (st.crosswalk), and occupies a carrier k (a lane, st.lane, or a roadway) across which it moves: drv.motion.moving_across_carrier(subject, k) with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance and cos_max p.crossing_motion_cos.
obligation: For each such carrier k, the subject moves at right angles to it: drv.motion.moving_across_carrier(subject, k) with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance and cos_max p.right_angle_crossing_cos.

narrowings.why: 'at right angles to the curb' and 'the shortest route to the opposite curb' are read as motion perpendicular, within p.right_angle_crossing_cos, to the designated direction of the lane or roadway the pedestrian occupies, which runs along the curb; where the curbs are not parallel the shortest route may differ from that perpendicular, and a roadway carrying no designated direction (an unlaned two-way roadway) leaves the duty unknown.

segmentation.text: Every pedestrian
crossing a roadway
at any point other than within a marked crosswalk or within an unmarked crosswalk at an intersection
shall yield
the right-of-way
to all vehicles upon the roadway
The foregoing rules in this Section shall have no application under the conditions stated in Section 11.30.070
when pedestrians are prohibited from crossing at certain designated places

elements.justification: 'pedestrian' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'); one atom.

Same words and reading as LVMC_11_30_050's 'shall cross a roadway': the pedestrian occupies a roadway (rel.occupies; st.roadway, 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder') and moves across a carrier k it occupies (a lane, st.lane, or the roadway): drv.motion.moving_across_carrier with cos_max p.crossing_motion_cos. The roadway so bound is r.

st.crosswalk, 'marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection', carries both the marked crosswalk and the unmarked crosswalk at an intersection (the defined crosswalk's two branches); the condition is that the pedestrian does not occupy one (rel.occupies).

Same words and meaning as the index's 'shall yield' -> kin.speed, rel.contact: the pedestrian grants precedence by not proceeding into a conflict; kin.speed, 'magnitude of velocity', tells whether it proceeds (above p.halt_speed_tolerance), and rel.contact, 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)', is the crash the yield secures against. Not a near miss: the near conflict is the standard's (f5).

'all vehicles' are members v of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, quantified in the obligation; 'upon the roadway' is 'the' roadway r the pedestrian crosses, re-bound in the obligation with its selection (the roadway the pedestrian occupies and crosses), and v occupies it (rel.occupies; st.roadway).

A place where pedestrians are prohibited from crossing is shown on the road by a posted prohibition: dev.regulatory_sign, 'a point regulation by catalogue code', code pedestrians_prohibited, governing (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') the roadway r the pedestrian crosses. 'designated' is legal status, read through the sign's presence. A prohibition sign is a condition, not a manoeuvre, as its contract says.

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way: precedence owed where direction, speed and proximity give rise to the danger of a crash
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: the defined right-of-way arises between road users 'approaching under such circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash'; that danger is read, from the two road users' directions, speeds and positions, as their centres approaching under constant velocities within p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) to a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance).

residues.why: Section 11.30.070 is no node of this run's library, neither accepted nor planned, so no rule can be composed; the condition under which it suspends this section is stated in this text's own words, 'when pedestrians are prohibited from crossing at certain designated places', carried by f8. Conditions of 11.30.070 those words do not state are not read; reported to the operator.

applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian; it occupies a roadway r and moves across a carrier k it occupies (a lane or the roadway; drv.motion.moving_across_carrier with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance and cos_max p.crossing_motion_cos); it occupies no crosswalk (st.crosswalk); and no dev.regulatory_sign of code pedestrians_prohibited governs (dev.governs) that roadway r.
obligation: For every vehicle v (DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) that occupies the roadway the subject occupies and crosses (re-bound with the same selection): the subject is not in contact with v (rel.contact), and it is not the case that the subject is moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) while the subject's and v's centres, under constant velocities, approach within p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) to a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance).

narrowings.why: 'shall yield' is read as not proceeding into a danger of a crash with a vehicle on the roadway: a pedestrian at rest yields, and one moving while no conflict with any vehicle is projected yields too.

the right-of-way's 'direction, speed and proximity' are read only through the constant-velocity closest approach of the two centres; a crash danger arising from acceleration within the horizon is not read.
a place designated as one where pedestrians are prohibited from crossing is read through the presence of a pedestrians_prohibited regulatory sign governing the roadway crossed.

contract: Road user a overtakes and passes road user b from the rear: a, travelling in the same direction as b, comes from having b ahead of it to having b behind it. b is ahead of a where the longitudinal component of b's bearing in a's frame (rel.bearing) is positive and the two bodies' projections on a's heading share no length (rel.longitudinal_overlap negative); b is behind a where that component is negative and the projections share no length. The act begins at the last observation of the window behind at which b was ahead of a with their headings aligned within same_dir_cos (rel.same_direction). The act is recognized at the observation at which b is behind a and was not behind a at the previous observation, where b was ahead of a with headings aligned at some observation of the window behind. The concept holds at that observation only, and not again until b has again been ahead of a and then comes to be behind it. Conduct before the window behind is not read: a pass that takes longer than the window is not recognized. It denotes the relative motion of the two road users only: it says nothing of the lanes they occupy, of whether b moves, or of why a passes. Not denoted: a drawing alongside b that does not clear b; b ahead of a only while their headings are not aligned (a road user met head-on or crossing); b behind a at every observation of the window.

params.name: window
params.meaning: the longest duration of a pass the concept recognizes: how far behind the observation it looks for b ahead of a

params.name: same_dir_cos
params.meaning: cosine of the largest heading difference at which a and b count as travelling in the same direction

act.onset: The act begins at the last observation of the window behind at which b was ahead of a with their headings aligned within same_dir_cos (rel.same_direction).
act.recognition: The act is recognized at the observation at which b is behind a and was not behind a at the previous observation, where b was ahead of a with headings aligned at some observation of the window behind.
act.extent: The concept holds at that observation only, and not again until b has again been ahead of a and then comes to be behind it.
act.history: Conduct before the window behind is not read: a pass that takes longer than the window is not recognized.

elements.span: the longitudinal component of b's bearing in a's frame (rel.bearing)
elements.justification: rel.bearing: 'direction of b from a in a's frame (for "on the right of", "immediately to the rear")'; its longitudinal component's sign tells b ahead of a from b behind it.

elements.span: the two bodies' projections on a's heading share no length (rel.longitudinal_overlap negative)
elements.justification: rel.longitudinal_overlap: 'the length the two footprints' projections on that axis share, negative for the gap between the projections'; a negative value means the bodies are not side by side, so a has cleared b (or not yet reached it). Used as a projection, not as a contact or a distance.

elements.span: with their headings aligned within same_dir_cos (rel.same_direction)
elements.justification: rel.same_direction: 'headings aligned: the cosine of the angle between the headings is above its tolerance', with the tolerance same_dir_cos; it tells an overtaking from a meeting or a crossing.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: a follows b in the same lane 15 m behind at 12 m/s while b is halted; a moves to the adjacent lane, draws alongside and, 4 s after b was last ahead of it, has b 3 m behind it: at that observation the concept holds.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: a follows b, moves to the adjacent lane and draws alongside b, then halts with the two bodies still side by side; b never comes to be behind a within the window.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: a draws past b in the adjacent lane, but the bearing of b from a is not observed.

contract: Road user a moves across the designated direction of travel of carrier region r: a is moving, its speed (kin.speed) above speed_tol, and its velocity (kin.velocity) makes with r's designated direction (st.lane_direction) an angle whose cosine, in absolute value, is at most cos_max: the absolute value of the dot product of the velocity with the normalised direction is at most cos_max times the speed. Either sense of crossing is denoted: the sign of the direction does not matter. It is a state at one observation: it says nothing of whether a occupies r, of where a began or will end its movement, or of how long it has moved so. Not denoted: a road user at rest or moving at or below speed_tol; a road user moving more nearly along r's direction than cos_max allows. Where r carries no designated direction, or a's velocity is not observed, it is unknown.

params.name: speed_tol
params.meaning: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement

params.name: cos_max
params.meaning: the largest absolute cosine between the velocity and the carrier's designated direction at which the motion counts as across the carrier

elements.justification: kin.speed: 'magnitude of velocity' (m/s); above speed_tol the road user is moving.
kin.velocity: 'velocity vector' (m/s, world frame); its dot product with the direction gives the motion along the carrier.
st.lane_direction: 'direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in — a lane, ... or a roadway', read normalised; a place no carrier covers has none (unknown).

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian on a lane whose direction is east walks north at 1.4 m/s: the dot product is zero, at most cos_max times the speed.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian on the same lane walks east along it at 1.4 m/s: the absolute cosine is 1, above cos_max.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian on the lane moves, but its velocity is not observed.
